questions.text: What is the shell register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: As in registers.map: DESIGN_ID 0x00, PKT_DATA 0x04, TICK 0x08, STATUS 0x0C, REPLY_LEN 0x10, REPLY_IDX 0x14, REPLY_WORD 0x18, TELE_LEN 0x1C, TELE_IDX 0x20, TELE_WORD 0x24, TAKE 0x28, all 32-bit.
questions.reason: The request names shell registers but gives no offsets.
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)

questions.text: The Nexys A7-100T oscillator is 100 MHz but the request says 125 MHz with an 8 ns constraint; which is meant?
questions.default: Use the 8 ns constraint as written, with CLKS_PER_BIT 1085.
questions.reason: The request is explicit about 125 MHz.
questions.answer: The spec settles it as 100 MHz with a 10 ns constraint, not 125 MHz with 8 ns. CLKS_PER_BIT stays 868, so the proposed default of 8 ns with CLKS_PER_BIT 1085 is not supported by the spec.

questions.text: How is the last flag given through the shell?
questions.default: Bit 8 of PKT_DATA is the last flag.
questions.answer: The end flag is bit 8 of register IN at offset 0x00 (write-only). The spec names that register IN, not PKT_DATA, so the proposed default's register name does not match the spec. Bits [7:0] carry the packet byte.

questions.text: Does a frame falling due in the same clock a held frame is taken count as dropped?
questions.default: Yes, dropped, since the frame is still held at that clock.
questions.answer: Yes, dropped, since the frame is still held at that clock.
